explanation: Breadth-first search records the predecessor of each first-discovered vertex. Reconstruct the route backward from the destination.
correctness: BFS discovers vertices in nondecreasing distance from start. A predecessor chain from first discovery therefore has minimum edge count; the visited set prevents cycling.
walkthrough: In the network a:{b,c}, b:{a,d}, c:{a,d}, d:{b,c}, breadth-first search visits b and c at distance 1 and discovers d at distance 2. Reconstructing via b gives [a,b,d]. The equally short route [a,c,d] is also valid; both contain two edges. JSON supplies an adjacency map and two endpoint labels. Return any shortest route including endpoints; the adapter accepts tied routes and a no-route result.
edgeCases: start=end returns [start]. A disconnected destination returns no route; tied shortest paths may use different valid predecessor choices.
timeComplexity: Expected O(V+E) time: each discovered vertex is enqueued once and each outgoing adjacency entry examined at most once; reconstruction visits at most V predecessors. Labels are treated as bounded-size hash keys.
spaceComplexity: O(V) auxiliary space for the queue and predecessor map, plus an O(V) result route.
